newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Weakening riel a concern, says top Cambodian banke.
newsitem.headline: Weakening riel a concern, says top Cambodian banke.

text.p: Cambodia's central bank chief said on Monday he was concerned about the depreciation of riel currency, which has lost seven percent against the dollar after fighting in the capital earlier this month.

Thor Peng Leath, governor of the National Bank of Cambodia, said the riel was trading at 3,000 to the dollar, compared with 2,800 before the fighting and ousting of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6 by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
"The riel depreciation is affected by two points -- the fighting of July 5-6 and the strength of the dollar," Thor Peng Leath told reporters on Monday.
"I'm concerned about the depreciation in the riel," he added.
A Finance Ministry official told Reuters the government was also concerned about inflation, which was up 10 percent month-on-month in July compared with June.
Year-on-year inflation stood at under seven percent before the recent strife in Cambodia.
Inflation was flat in June compared with the previous month and up only 0.7 percent in May compared with April.4
